The Welsh-Indian film-maker’s work, which incorporates themes of memory, migration and hidden histories, was praised by judges for its “restless will to play, experiment and change”. items.title: Outcry grows over Labour plan to exempt most brownfield sites from nature protection rules
items.desc: Chancellor’s decision to exempt plots up to 1.5 hectares allows developers to dodge rules aiming to reverse wildlife declines An outcry is growing over the UK chancellor’s removal of most brownfield housing plots from a legal requirement for developers to measurably enhance nature. John Healey’s decision in the budget to exempt brownfield plots of up to 1.5 hectares from biodiversity net gain (BNG) laws effectively means housing developers of inner-city, urban and surburban sites will be able to dodge rules designed to reverse steep wildlife declines while also allowing housebuilding growth. According to government data, 86% of brownfield sites currently registered are 1.5ha or under. Continue reading...

items.title: Ministers approve fast-track disability payments in England and Wales

The Department for Work and Pensions said on Tuesday it would immediately commit to speeding up the personal independence payment (Pip) system for adults in England and Wales who have severe conditions or ones that are unlikely to change. items.title: ‘It was a cover-up’: HarperCollins accused of using lawyers to shut down concerns about David Walliams
items.desc: Women who spoke to internal investigation about inappropriate behaviour by Walliams still too scared to speak out The publisher HarperCollins used a leading legal firm and a non-disclosure agreement to “cover up” David Walliams’ inappropriate behaviour towards women two years before the children’s author was unexpectedly dropped, according to former staff. Women had complained to the company’s management for years about the author’s alleged misconduct and harassment. The concerns raised included that Walliams had an “inappropriate” sexual relationship with a woman who was an intern when he first met her, had inappropriate interactions with at least three other women connected to the company including asking two for dates, and approached a girl who appeared to be in her teens at a book signing event. Continue reading...
